(2) Independently, cutting feed-water flow to zero restored titer to ~65, while high feed flow (30) left titer at ~30, pinpointing the feed water as the contamination source. (3) The operators' leading theories were ruled out: DO was flat (~55) across conditions and temperature/antifoam had no effect. (4) Broth turbidity correlated only weakly with titer (r=-0.58) and dropped alongside chelation — it is a bystander driven by the same metal, not the cause. Recommended fix: chelator at ~65 to neutralize the leached metal, and address/replace the feed-water fitting (reducing feed-water contamination) to remove the source.
